prerequisites: Knowledge across the breadth of the studied subject

learning_outcomes.text: Students can methodically process practical tasks and present them within a given timeframe with a clearly structured result.

Students possess a critical understanding of the most important theories, principles, and methods from their studies, can apply this basis to a new task, and independently deepen their knowledge in a specific area.
Students can evaluate the state of the literature in the context of the underlying research question and critically reflect on methodical approaches.

Students use the tools and methods learned and developed during their studies to support their work. On this basis, they develop solution approaches and realize solutions that correspond to the state of science.

Students research the state of the art and science and derive innovative approaches to the specific scientific task of their thesis. In their elaborations, they present the underlying research results and their innovations.

Students formulate identified technical challenges and solutions, classify them into an interdisciplinary context, and present them in discourse with subject matter experts. They communicate with stakeholders and consider their diverse perspectives and areas of interest.

In their thesis, students develop a professional self-image oriented towards the goals and standards of professional action in professional fields predominantly outside of academia. They recognize situationally appropriate conditions for professional action concerning the task of their thesis and can reflect on their activity in an interdisciplinary context.

syllabus_topics: Recording the state of the art
Developing concepts for solving the task
Developing partial solutions and assembling them into an overall concept
Overall consideration and evaluation of the solution
Presenting the solution in the form of the bachelor thesis
Presenting the results within a colloquium
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance consists of the final thesis and the colloquium. 12 ECTS are awarded for the Bachelor thesis and 3 ECTS for the colloquium. The Bachelor thesis should be 40-70 pages long. The colloquium lasts 15-45 minutes.
